description: Sandbox cargo incremental rebuild is unreliable: after editing a test file, nextest re-ran a stale binary and re-emitted OLD failure text (run 01M336MYEF1R5C1JMC6WHFTCQY, seeds-540e); touch was not always enough — cargo clean -p <crate> reliably forced the rebuild. Always suspect a stale binary when a just-fixed assertion fails identically.
resolution: cargo clean -p seeds then rerun; full verify green afterward

name: serde-json-preserve-order-remove-is-swap-remove
description: serde_json Map::remove with preserve_order is swap_remove: deleting a mid-record field silently reorders remaining keys (last key moves into the hole), diverging from sd's stable in-place deletion. Use shift_remove for order-stable field deletion in tracker records (seeds model.rs remove_field, run 01M338CGYHE24Y5KXBXMB8DJWR).

name: cli-to-library-command-lift
description: seeds-0dfd: lifting a CLI command layer into a library API with byte-stable output works with a CommandOutcome{success,stdout,stderr} return (no printing, no process::exit library-side), a CommandContext::at(dir)/from_cwd() split for compile-in vs cwd resolution, and pub-field+Default input structs — #[non_exhaustive] on inputs must be avoided because it blocks cross-crate struct literals, which is the exact compile-in use; pin byte-stability with a before/after scratch-store battery diffed parse-level before any refactor

Engine checkout leaves workspace source files with epoch (1970) mtimes, so cargo considers previously-built artifacts fresh and silently skips rebuild after edits — a re-run then executes a stale binary and re-emits old behavior (run 01M39RPNKNAH1FE2998A44XKD5, seeds-de37).
resolution: After editing, touch the touched .rs files (or cargo clean -p <crate>) before re-running the binary or tests; treat a suspiciously instant rebuild as a stale-binary signal.

name: ring-musl-cross-cc-conventions
description: ring (rustls crypto) on musl targets demands target-conventional C compiler names via cc-rs: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl wants x86_64-linux-musl-gcc (fix: CC_x86_64_unknown_linux_musl=cc + AR=ar with host gcc - ring C is freestanding), aarch64-unknown-linux-musl wants aarch64-linux-musl-gcc (CI: apt gcc-aarch64-linux-gnu + CC_aarch64_unknown_linux_musl=aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc). Linker stays rust-lld (self-contained; system ld fails on --fix-cortex-a53-843419). Verified in seeds release pipeline runs 36230738000/36230842988 and locally with musl.cc toolchain (seeds-bdcb, 2026-09-26).

name: std-file-try-lock-advisory-locking
description: std::fs::File::try_lock/lock (stabilized Rust 1.89, verified on 1.98) gives flock-semantics advisory file locking with RAII-on-File: the lock lives on the open file description, drops with the File, and the kernel releases it on process death (crash-safe, no stale-lockfile machinery) — replaces fs4/fd-lock entirely when a wrapper crate is only needed for locking. Two verified properties: separate open file descriptions of the SAME file conflict within one process (WouldBlock), enabling in-process thread tests of cross-process semantics; and poll try_lock + sleep is the timeout recipe (blocking lock() has no deadline). Pitfall avoided: fd_lock-style guard types borrow their lock (self-referential if stored together) — the std File-owned model composes into a plain struct field (seeds-0d7b, lock.rs).

name: pace-metrics-clock-injection
description: stats --pace (seeds-8fc5): deterministic time-series metrics need an injected clock as a library seam (PaceOptions.now, no CLI flag) plus exact integer ETA arithmetic (open*window div_ceil closures) — float ceil() hit 20.000000000000004 and would have shipped an off-by-one date; pattern: keep rate math in f64 for display, fold projections back to integers.
